source: Source: Univ. of Bath, PLOS Biology (Nov 2026)

scenes.vo: Since nineteen seventy two, a popular idea said your most important genes were protected from mutation. A new study says no.
scenes.cap: Since 1972: 'important genes mutate less.' A new study says no.

scenes.vo: The idea: genes a cell can't live without mutate less. Like keeping your passport in a safe.
scenes.cap: The idea: essential genes get fewer mutations, like a passport in a safe

scenes.vo: The University of Bath tested it with the largest collection of spontaneous mutations so far.
scenes.cap: University of Bath: largest collection of spontaneous mutations so far

scenes.vo: Two species. E. coli bacteria, and baker's yeast.
scenes.cap: Tested in E. coli and baker's yeast

scenes.vo: Result: essential genes did not mutate any less. Not in either species.
scenes.cap: Essential genes did NOT mutate less in either species

scenes.vo: Why did older studies see protection? Harmful mutations in vital genes kill the cell before they're counted. Ghost mutations.
scenes.cap: Harmful mutations get removed before they're counted: 'ghost mutations'

scenes.vo: Caveat: only two microbes so far. Mutation is random, selection is not. So, are your genes protected? Not the way we thought since nineteen seventy two.
scenes.cap: Caveat: 2 microbes only. Mutation is random, selection is not.
